prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CCS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(CC(=O)Nc2nc(-c3cccc(Cl)c3)c(C(=O)c3ccccc3Cl)s2)cc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL1741186

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of APC-labeled RORgammat receptor ligand binding domain (unknown origin) after 1 hr by FRET assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Displacement of [3H]-2-(4-(ethylsulfonyl)phenyl)-N-(4-(2-(methoxymethyl)phenyl)thiophen-2-yl)acetamide from purified N-(HN)6-GST-TCS-human RORgammat (258 to 518 residues) incubated for 16 hrs by scintillation proximity assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.55, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "The two assays use fundamentally different detection methods (FRET-based cofactor recruitment vs. radioligand displacement SPA) with different incubation times (1 hr vs. 16 hrs) and measure different binding events, which can lead to IC50 values differing by more than 1 log unit even for the same compound and target."}

parsed.reason: The two assays use fundamentally different detection methods (FRET-based cofactor recruitment vs. radioligand displacement SPA) with different incubation times (1 hr vs. 16 hrs) and measure different binding events, which can lead to IC50 values differing by more than 1 log unit even for the same compound and target.
